lessons.title: Inside the Village of Longevity

lessons.key_idea: The Okinawan habit of hara hachi bu, stopping before you are full and eating a varied, plant-rich diet, is one simple pillar of a long life.

lessons.title: Lose Yourself in Flow

lessons.title: Find Meaning, Accept Your Feelings
lessons.key_idea: Logotherapy helps you discover what gives your life meaning, while Morita therapy teaches you to accept your emotions and act purposefully anyway.

lessons.title: Keep Moving, Gently, Every Day
lessons.key_idea: Long-lived people rarely do intense workouts but move naturally all day, and gentle practices like radio taiso, tai chi or yoga keep body and mind healthy.

lessons.title: Bend Without Breaking, Live Your Ikigai
lessons.key_idea: Resilience, embracing imperfection and savouring each moment bring together purpose, community, food, flow and movement into a way of living your ikigai for the long run.

plan.title: Ikigai
plan.author: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles
plan.confidence_note: I know the book's main concepts, structure and the Okinawa village research well, though I would avoid quoting specific interviewees or figures without checking.
plan.one_liner: Why do some Okinawans live past 100, smiling? Their secret might be a reason to get up.
plan.summary: Why do so many people on the Japanese island of Okinawa live past 100, and stay cheerful doing it? Héctor García and Francesc Miralles set out to find out, visiting the rural village of Ogimi and talking with its oldest residents. Their answer centres on ikigai, a Japanese idea that roughly means your reason for getting up in the morning. The book blends those interviews with everyday habits and ideas from psychology. It covers eating until you are about 80 percent full, moving gently every day, and staying close to friends and community. It draws on Viktor Frankl's logotherapy and Japanese Morita therapy to explore meaning, and on the idea of flow to show how absorbing activities keep us engaged. It ends with resilience, embracing imperfection, and ten simple rules for living a long, purposeful life.
